0.content: Jean is Barbara's older sister. When their parents separated, Jean stayed with their mother Frederica and was trained as the Gunnhildr heir; Barbara stayed with their father. Jean has always wanted to get closer but cannot find the words when Barbara's eyes slide away, and Barbara behaves the same way. Barbara tried all her life to beat Jean at one thing, whether swords or grades, and never managed it. She still admires her and wishes she could lighten her load. Jean thinks Barbara is "too hard on herself", and knows it because the Knights also oversee the Church.

1.comment: Barbara: Seamus Pegg and Frederica Gunnhildr
1.content: Barbara's father Seamus Pegg was once a famous adventurer who started over in Mondstadt's Church and rose to Seneschal, known as the Cardinal of Daybreak. He raised Barbara, was surprised by her determination, and counselled her to become a healer. Her mother Frederica Gunnhildr is a veteran knight of the Gunnhildr Clan who raised Jean. Both parents left with Grand Master Varka's expedition; Seamus handed his Church duties to Cardinal Calvin, and Barbara has prayed for their safe return.

2.comment: Barbara: Alice and the Idol Magazine
2.content: Barbara first heard the word "idol" from Alice, an elder of the Hexenzirkel. Confused that anyone but The Seven could be worshipped, she was handed an "Idol Magazine" from some unknown world and learned that idols work hard to be liked and can heal people's spirits through song and dance. She threw herself into learning songs and found happiness in others' smiles. When Alice's plans for "Teyvat Idols!" collapsed, Barbara decided she would define what an idol is herself. She repeats Alice's maxim that a true idol tries to heal the souls of the people.

3.comment: Barbara: Venti and the Holy Lyre
3.content: At the end of the Prologue (1.0) Barbara came to collect the Holy Lyre der Himmel, the Church relic the Traveler and Venti had borrowed. Its broken state made her scream and swear that a lifetime of penance would not be enough. Venti quietly "repaired" it with Anemo, and she snatched it back, forbidding them ever to touch it again. Minutes later she found the Traveler unconscious outside the Cathedral after Signora's attack and healed them. Her powers had almost no effect on Venti, who called it "completely normal" and left for Windrise.

4.content: Rosaria is the Church's most absent sister, and Barbara is the one person who keeps trying to reach her: reminding her not to smoke in the Cathedral, chasing her to services and choir practice. Rosaria calls her a thorn in her side and suspects Victoria set Barbara to watch her. Barbara admits she has not quite found the courage to really talk to her, and insists Rosaria surely believes in the Anemo Archon.

5.content: Dahlia is a fellow deacon. Barbara looks up to him because he brings the word of Barbatos to the clergy, and notes he is hard to find, preferring markets and taverns to the quiet Cathedral. Dahlia calls her a friend who is always there to support him, and deliberately asks her for help because helping makes her happiest. It was Dahlia who once had Barbara fetch Rosaria for choir practice.

6.comment: Barbara: Bennett and the Adhesive Bandages
6.content: Bennett is at the Cathedral so often with fractures and dislocations that even Barbara is surprised at how skilled he has become at popping joints back in. She tells him he should take better care of himself. When he apologises ("Sorry, it's me again..."), she shakes her head and tosses him adhesive bandages "for those scratches as well". Bennett treasures them like medals. He goes to her concerts after bad adventures and envies her popularity.

7.comment: Barbara: The Barbara Fan Club and Sister Victoria
7.content: Albert, a citizen who lingers at the Cathedral doors, leads the Barbara Fan Club, "the biggest club for Barbara-sama fans in all of Mondstadt". The nuns keep chasing him off; the senior nun Victoria distrusts him without knowing he is only a fan. Barbara once scolded him for humming her songs out of tune. Victoria, who listens to confessions and watches over the younger clergy, makes Barbara report where she is going so the Church can rescue her from crowds, and wishes she would stop overworking.
